column4: the CDC stability law ("every chunk at least 2 x max past the insertion re-appears") is an empirical property of high-entropy content, not a guarantee: zero runs, short periods and zero-run noise force max-length cuts that do not re-synchronise; the end-of-input chunk must not count as "before the insertion" when the byte is appended at the end (it was cut by the input end, not by content); the dump records per-insertion counts on both sides and the gate is byte identity, the law is reported per content kind
column5: pass 1 counted 335 insertions beyond 2 x max incl. tiny files with the byte appended at the end; classification fixed (end <= position and end < length)
